title: IC Manager Toolbox and Ladder Playbook
author: Rina Sharma
content:
SUMMARY
This document describes the 'IC Manager Toolbox' — a curated set of internal tools, permissions, workflows, and career-mapping guidance that enable individual contributors (ICs) to take on manager-like responsibilities for projects, mentoring, and operational ownership without a formal manager title. The playbook explains how ICs get access to tooling, how responsibilities map to career ladders, promotion criteria, and how benefits and perks align with expanded scope.

PURPOSE
- Reduce friction for cross-functional IC ownership (tech leads, project owners, on-call leads) by standardizing access and expectations.
- Make role progression transparent: what skills, deliverables, and operational scope are expected at each IC level when operating with manager responsibilities.
- Preserve clarity between line management duties and IC leadership activities; offer safety rails and escalation paths.

SCOPE AND AUDIENCE
This playbook is for: software engineers, ML engineers, product managers working as ICs, people managers who approve elevated IC privileges, and People Ops. It covers tooling access, permission templates, 90-day onboarding checklists, promotion rubrics, and benefit eligibility related to expanded role scope.

IC MANAGER TOOLBOX — WHAT IT IS
The IC Manager Toolbox is a package of tools and permissions that are granted as a single bundle when an IC is approved for expanded scope for a defined period. Typical capabilities included:
- Project workspace creation and lifecycle ownership in Confluence and Jira.
- Team-level on-call rotation assignment and the ability to create runbooks.
- Budget view-only for assigned feature flags/allocated infra through the Cost Console.
- Ability to create private RFCs and propose policy changes.
- Mentorship hours allocation (formal 1:1 slots and mentee assignments).
- Hiring interview scheduling privileges (panel invites) and interview feedback templates.

TOOLING INVENTORY (QUICK REFERENCE)
| Tool | Purpose | Default Owner | Access Process | Notes |
|-------|---------|---------------|----------------|-------|
| Confluence Team Space | Project docs & runbooks | Eng Platform | Request via "/access create-space" ticket | Template: ic-team-space-v1 |
| Jira Project (read/write) | Task/issue ownership | Eng Platform | People Ops approval + manager signoff | Use board template: feature-owner-board |
| On-call roster manager | Roster edits, runbook updates | SRE | Pager duty group grant | Scoped to services assigned |
| Cost Console (view) | Budget transparency | Finance Ops | Audit request: cost-console-view | No charge modification |
| Interview Scheduler | Candidate scheduling | Recruiting | Self-assign after panel approval | Use interview feedback template |

ACCESS AND APPROVAL WORKFLOW (NUMBERS)
1. Nomination: IC or manager submits an IC Manager Toolbox nomination form (short form: why, scope, duration, expected outcomes).
2. Manager endorsement: direct manager provides endorsement + lists collaborators and expected time allocation.
3. People Ops review: confirms policy alignment, checks capacity and benefit eligibility.
4. Tooling grant: Eng Platform / SRE / Finance apply scoped permissions (7 business days target).
5. Confirmation kickoff: People Ops schedules 30-minute kickoff with IC, manager, and tooling owners.

Sample nomination checklist (to attach to form):
- Objective and target impact (200–400 words)
- Expected duration (3 / 6 / 12 months)
- Time allocation estimate (e.g., 20% mentorship / 10% interviews / 70% IC work)
- List of services or projects in scope
- Manager endorsement (name and signature)

ONBOARDING CHECKLIST (FIRST 90 DAYS)
1. Day 0–3: Confirm toolbox access, create project Confluence space, and import runbook template.
2. Week 1: Hold kickoff meeting with stakeholders; publish 90-day plan on Confluence.
3. Week 2–4: Shadow current on-call lead or manager for operational handover.
4. Month 1: Update runbook, set up monitoring alerts (with SRE assistance), and schedule biweekly mentor office hours.
5. Month 2: Lead first project retro and write a short process RFC for one internal workflow.
6. Month 3: Submit self-assessment against the IC leadership rubric; manager and reviewer provide feedback.

IC LEADERSHIP AND PROMOTION RUBRIC (OVERVIEW)
Promotion decisions that consider manager-like responsibilities use the standard IC ladder plus three operational axes:
- Delivery & technical impact (feature ownership, cross-team outcomes).
- People leadership (mentorship quality, interview impact, cross-team coordination).
- Operational ownership (incidence handling, runbook completeness, cost optimization).

Scoring guidance (used in calibration, simplified for transparency):
- Meets expectations: consistently reliable delivery, contributes to team health, maintains runbooks.
- Exceeds expectations: leads cross-team initiatives, mentors multiple ICs, drives cost or reliability improvements.
- Exceptional: sustained organizational impact, repeatable mentoring outcomes, recognized as go-to lead for service area.

PROMOTION CHECKLIST (SAMPLE)
- 2+ demonstrated end-to-end projects with measurable impact (KPIs defined).
- 6+ months of consistent mentorship/leadership activity and documented mentee outcomes.
- Clear operational ownership: runbooks updated, SLA/SLO observability checks in place.
- Peer and manager endorsements (2–4 reviewers recommended).
- Up-to-date career mapping document and manager-derived competency examples.

BENEFITS & PERKS ALIGNMENT
ICs with Toolbox privileges become eligible for a set of role-expansion benefits while retaining IC employment terms. Benefit eligibility examples:
- Leadership Stipend: a monthly $250 stipend to support team-building (offsite snacks, swag, books).
- Mentorship Hours Bank: up to 4 hours/week of protected time for mentoring and interviews (tracked in weekly capacity).
- Professional Development Boost: $2,000/year training allowance for leadership or coaching classes in addition to baseline L&D.
- Ergonomics/Hybrid Office Upgrade: one-time $600 allowance when increased coordination is required (team hubs, extended travel).
These benefits are granted for the approved duration and reviewed at the end of the term for continuation.

PERMISSION SCAFFOLD (EXAMPLE TABLE)
| Permission | When granted | Scope | Revocation condition |
|-----------|--------------|-------|----------------------|
| Jira Project Admin (limited) | On approval | Only for assigned project boards | Project handover or end date |
| Confluence Space Admin | On approval | Own project space templates | Major policy violation or end date |
| On-call roster edit | After shadowing | Services assigned only | If operational errors exceed thresholds |

ESCALATION & GUARDRAILS
- ICs are not line managers by default. This playbook does not change headcount or performance management responsibilities. Any direct reports remain the manager's responsibility.
- If an IC needs to perform personnel actions (e.g., formal performance feedback, salary discussions), they must escalate to People Ops and the direct manager.
- Operational error threshold: 3 unmitigated incidents in a 6-month period where runbooks or monitoring were not followed will trigger a review and potential temporary revocation of toolbox privileges.

INTERNAL TOOLS QUICK REFERENCE AND CONTACTS
- Eng Platform: eng-platform@redwood.com — responsible for Confluence/Jira templates and access grants.
- SRE: sre@redwood.com — runbook reviews, on-call onboarding, monitoring.
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.com — nominations, benefit approvals, conflict resolution.
- Finance Ops: finance-ops@redwood.com — cost console view grants and budget questions.

TEMPLATES AND EXAMPLES (SNIPPETS)
Nomination form example (paste into the nomination portal):
{
  "applicant": "<your name>",
  "objective": "Lead rollout of streaming cache for search service — reduce p99 by 30%",
  "duration": "6 months",
  "manager_endorsement": "<manager name>",
  "time_allocation": "20%",
  "services_in_scope": ["search-api", "cache-layer"]
}

Runbook checklist (minimum required items):
- Service owner and escalation path
- Health dashboards and thresholds
- Common mitigation steps (ops playbook)
- Post-incident follow-up template

OWNERSHIP, REVIEW CYCLE, AND EXCEPTIONS
- Owner: People Ops maintains this playbook; Eng Platform, SRE, and Finance Ops operate the underlying tooling.
- Review cadence: Annual review every Q1 with ad-hoc updates for platform changes.
- Exceptions: Request exception via People Ops; all exceptions must include a rollback plan and defined expiry.

APPENDIX (PROMOTION TEMPLATE CHECKLIST)
1) Impact summary (one page)
2) Measurable outcomes (metrics and dates)
3) Manager endorsement and time allocation confirmation
4) 2–4 peer reviewers with short statements
5) Updated career mapping document
